headline: ClinGeX reports improved clinical-genomics concordance with executable domain skills and clinician collaboration
summary: An arXiv paper introduces ClinGeX, a clinical-genomics agent organized around 105 executable skills selected and sequenced for each task. The authors report 71.7% macro-averaged task-level concordance across 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, compared with 45.7% for the strongest comparator. In a counterbalanced study across three centres, 45 clinical-genomics professionals completed 135 cases with ClinGeX, DeepSeek or no AI assistance; ClinGeX-assisted concordance was higher in all three scenarios. A separate one-month assessment collected 96 self-selected analysis-episode reports from 11 professionals, who reported frequent conclusion adoption and shorter analysis time. The real-use assessment was non-interventional and outputs could not affect patient care. All performance and workflow results remain author-reported; no independent reproduction or clinical-outcome trial was established.
